fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Night-time conspicuity of a HAWK display against competing background elements is a substantive, scheme-relevant safety issue affecting stop-decision reliability at a pedestrian crossing.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim is directly supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US-001 ('Drivers may be confused by competing background visual elements at night' at Speedway Blvd/Rook Ave), exceeding registry-id-only citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern rather than a compliance question, consistent with FHWA RSA semantics where findings are observational and non-normative (normative_basis_note appropriately null).
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reflective border installation is specific, actionable, and viable at final design stage, and aligns with recognized signal-conspicuity countermeasures, though it only partially mitigates background clutter.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians are explicitly identified as the exposed road users, with the driver-confusion-to-pedestrian-risk link clearly articulated, satisfying VRU consideration where relevant.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance adequacy for slower walkers at HAWK crossings on the corridor's highest pedestrian/bicycle collision sites is a genuine, well-recognized VRU safety issue at final design.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Verbatim quote EV-US-016 ('The pedestrian clearance interval may be short, particularly for elderly pedestrians') directly supports the pivotal claim and matches the recorded case-study issue cited in the confidence basis.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern phrased as a verification question rather than a compliance assertion, keeping safety and compliance categorically distinct per FHWA RSA semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: reprogramme clearance intervals at all six named HAWK sites using a reduced assumed walking speed, a standard viable MUTCD-consistent remedy; not null.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRU impact is the explicit core of the finding—elderly pedestrians are named in road_users, scenario, and evidence, fully addressing vulnerable-user exposure.
